correctness.rationale: Direct shore occupancy gives 2-dominance iff (a=s or b>=2) and (b=t or a>=2). Pre-existing theorem C2(K_s,t)=t+1 for 3<=s<=5 gives exact excess s-1<=4, so all possible nonsingleton block multisets are finitely enumerable. Independent complete occupancy enumeration for twelve required base (s,t) pairs returns exactly 1,2,4 templates: s3 (2,1); s4 (3,1) or ((2,0),(2,1)); s5 (4,1), ((2,0),(3,1)), ((2,1),(3,0)), ((1,2),(2,1)). For t>=2(s-1)+2 any two blocks combined cannot cover all B and >=2 B-singletons remain, so same templates stabilize; this is the nonfinite step. Falling-factorial label counts give 3t,10t,25t+15t(t-1)(t-2), with every block unlabeled and every vertex labeled. Verified finite template candidates independently; the established numeric optimum is used with credit, not claimed new.

evidence: Brešar et al established C2(K_s,t) over a broader (s,t) range than this claim but not the optimizer enumeration.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader parameter coverage of the scalar optimum cannot mechanically entail labeled multiplicities; the new theorem is a strictly finer invariant in three infinite small-shore regimes.

originality.rationale: Brešar–Henning–Samadi Theorem5.2 already solves the numerical 2-coalition number C2(K_s,t) for all bicliques and constructs witness partitions; the original scalar claim is fully covered. Its proof does not give the exhaustive optimizing occupancy profiles or labeled multiplicity counts for s=3,4,5. Jafari–Alikhani–Bakhshesh defines k-coalitions, while double-coalition literature uses different domination. A well-motivated structural/enumerative refinement remains original under inspected source coverage, with unindexed enumerator risk.
residual_risks: Only s in {3,4,5}, t>=s+1, k=2; not balanced shores or general larger s, not nonoptimal partitions.
